solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: Understate personal record recalled in diary regularly (8)

indicators.note: called back, so the record is read backwards
the pieces sit inside the diary letters
something done regularly happens at even intervals, so letters are taken at even intervals: every other one

blocks.note: first of the alternate letters D, A, Y
the rest of D-A-Y from dIaRy's odd letters

annotation.surface: Someone keeps a diary but plays down their own achievements in it.
annotation.walkthrough: The odd letters of diary give DAY, which opens up to hold OWN and a backwards LP.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: making a thing seem less important than it is, playing it down.

entries.clue: Give information in flyer after shop is planned (10)

indicators.note: the informer's word goes inside the flyer
the shop comes first, the rest after it

blocks.note: to rat is to inform on someone

annotation.surface: A shop owner advertises through a leaflet that was carefully planned.
annotation.walkthrough: The flyer is not a leaflet but a flying insect, the BEE, which swallows RAT.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: done on purpose and thought out in advance.

entries.clue: Sketch this accomplishment of Victor wearing drag (3)

indicators.note: DRAG wears the answer, wrapping round it

blocks.note: the answer itself, which goes inside DRAG
the word that wears the answer; the result is the sketch
what DRAG makes once it wears the answer: a picture, not a comedy routine

annotation.surface: A comedy sketch in which a man called Victor performs in drag.
annotation.walkthrough: A reverse clue: put this answer inside DRAG and you get DRAWING, a sketch. The capital on Victor hides that a victor's accomplishment is simply a win.
annotation.definitionFit: A victor is by definition someone who has triumphed, so a victory is the one accomplishment every victor shares.

entries.clue: Ask spy source in enemy complex for means of access (7)

indicators.note: the source of a word is its first letter
the letters are tangled up

annotation.surface: An agent is asked to find a way into an enemy compound.
annotation.walkthrough: Complex looks like a noun, a building, but it tells you to rearrange ASK SPY E.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: a master key that opens many locks lets you in.

entries.clue: Proceed to block some files for advisory panels? (5,7)

indicators.note: GO blocks, sitting inside, the other word

blocks.note: soldiers in files march in columns

annotation.surface: An instruction to go and hold up some documents meant for advisory committees.
annotation.walkthrough: Agony columns are newspaper advice pages, where an agony aunt answers readers' problems; the question mark admits calling them panels is a stretch.
annotation.definitionFit: A playful definition: newspaper advice pages sit in boxed panels of print, and their whole job is advising.

entries.clue: Unethical counterpart to PM against test (6)

blocks.note: morning is the counterpart of p.m.

annotation.surface: An unethical rival of the Prime Minister opposes some test.
annotation.walkthrough: PM reads as Prime Minister, but it is the time of day, whose counterpart is AM.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: lacking any moral sense at all is unethical.

entries.clue: US subject receives award for drama (7)

indicators.note: the subject takes the award inside it

blocks.note: MATH, the American word for maths: first part
Commander of the Order of the British Empire, an honour

annotation.surface: An American subject of study wins a prize for drama.
annotation.walkthrough: The CBE is a British honour given by the monarch.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: Shakespeare's Scottish tragedy is one drama among many.

entries.clue: Old dominion’s premier confused about sultanate (5,6)

indicators.note: the letters of premier are jumbled
they go round the sultanate

blocks.note: PREMIER jumbled to R + EMPIRE: first letter
Oman is ruled by a sultan

annotation.surface: A former dominion's prime minister is baffled by a sultanate.
annotation.walkthrough: The apostrophe s joins definition to wordplay as 'has'.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: the realm ruled from Rome is an ancient territory under one power.

entries.clue: Dash with leader going down passage (4)

indicators.note: the first letter drops to the bottom of this down entry

annotation.surface: Someone dashes, head down, along an alley.
annotation.walkthrough: In a down answer, 'going down' moves the E of ELAN from top to bottom.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a narrow way between hedges or buildings that you pass along.

entries.clue: Small possibility left about ghost materialising in new form (4,4)

indicators.note: the ghost's letters take a new shape

annotation.surface: There is only a slim chance that a ghost will appear in some new form.
annotation.walkthrough: About is ON, as in a book on birds, not a sign to put one thing round another.
annotation.definitionFit: An idiom from betting: an outsider at long odds has only a small chance.

entries.clue: Wisdom and totally unlimited tact mums deny (6)

indicators.note: every word loses its limits, its first and last letters

annotation.surface: Mothers refuse to show any tact or wisdom at all.
annotation.walkthrough: Totally applies to all three words: each loses its first and last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: A near synonym: keen, shrewd judgement is a kind of wisdom.

entries.clue: Corruption, masked in flattery, disheartened the king (12)

indicators.note: the pieces are hidden inside the flattery
the heart, the middle letter, is removed

blocks.note: THE without its middle letter H

annotation.surface: Moral decay lies hidden under the fawning praise that has taken the king's spirit.
annotation.walkthrough: Disheartened applies only to 'the', and king is R from the Latin rex.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: debasing something pure by mixing in impurities corrupts it.

entries.clue: Bruising ultimately affected head and pulse (5-4,4)

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the end of affected, its last letter, is used

annotation.surface: A bruise ended up affecting someone's head and their heart rate.
annotation.walkthrough: Pulse looks like a heartbeat, but here it is the food: peas, beans and lentils are pulses.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: pulses are the dried edible seeds of legumes, and this bean is one.

entries.clue: Sweet basil and leek nearly prepared (7,4)

indicators.note: leek loses its last letter
the letters are worked into a new form, as food is prepared

annotation.surface: A cook mixes sweet basil with leeks in a recipe.
annotation.walkthrough: Sweet basil is a real herb, so Sweet seems part of the ingredient list; it is the definition. An aniseed ball is a hard British sweet, a candy.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a small, hard, liquorice-flavoured British candy.

entries.clue: Not feeling excited, one entering in hospital department (10)

indicators.note: these letters go into the ones that follow

annotation.surface: A numb patient, unmoved, is admitted to a hospital department.
annotation.walkthrough: Excited as SENT is the older sense of being carried away, as in 'the music sent me'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: without sensation or consciousness.

entries.clue: Wet beam joint in auditorium (5)

indicators.note: in a hall the words are heard, not seen

blocks.note: a ray of light plus a knee joint

annotation.surface: A damp timber joist in a concert hall.
annotation.walkthrough: Beam and joint read like carpentry, but they are a ray of light and a knee.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym for weather with rain falling.

entries.clue: American article on holm oak revised (9)

indicators.note: a revised text has been rewritten into a new version, so the letters are rewritten into a new order

annotation.surface: An American writes a revised article about the holm oak tree.
annotation.walkthrough: The holm oak is an evergreen tree; here it is just letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: a native of one US state is an American.

entries.clue: Tense local abandoning female’s lofty abode (4-5)

indicators.note: the pub leaves the F behind

annotation.surface: A nervous local moves out of a woman's grand house.
annotation.walkthrough: A local is a neighbourhood pub, and a free house is a British pub not tied to one brewery. The 's is 'has', a link.
annotation.definitionFit: Literal and playful: a den built up in the branches is an abode that is lofty in the sense of high.

entries.clue: Prisoner I’m surprised turned on old coach (7)

indicators.note: the exclamation is turned round
in a down answer it sits on top of the next piece

annotation.surface: A captive is startled to find himself on board an antique stagecoach.
annotation.walkthrough: A stage was the old horse-drawn coach running between stages of a route.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by example: someone held captive as security for a demand is a prisoner.

entries.clue: Attack keep — insurgents held back guards (5)

indicators.note: the letters read backwards
the words guard the answer inside them

annotation.surface: Rebels holed up in a castle keep defend it against assault.
annotation.walkthrough: Keep is a castle tower in the surface, but only its last two letters matter.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: shooting from cover, or making sly critical remarks, both attack.

entries.clue: Ooze from spot on side (7)

annotation.surface: Liquid seeps from a stain on one side.
annotation.walkthrough: Spot suggests a stain, which fits ooze, but it is the verb: to see.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both nouns name a slow leak of liquid through something.

entries.clue: Withdrawal police officers promise (13)

annotation.surface: Police officers pledge to pull back.
annotation.walkthrough: DI is a Detective Inspector in British police ranks.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, especially military: pulling troops back out of contact with the enemy.

entries.clue: Case lost in African expedition miles away (4)

indicators.note: the outer letters, the case, are removed

blocks.note: SAFARI without its outer letters S and I

annotation.surface: A suitcase goes missing on a safari, far from home.
annotation.walkthrough: An African expedition is a safari.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: an adverb for at a great distance.

entries.clue: Dispute when behind vehicle loudly reversed (6)

indicators.note: this piece comes after the rest
the vehicle and the loud sign are read backwards

annotation.surface: A row breaks out when a car behind honks noisily as it backs up.
annotation.walkthrough: Loudly is F, forte in music.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a noisy quarrel or brawl.

entries.clue: Secure advanced warning and protective cover (8)

annotation.surface: Get an early warning and some protection.
annotation.walkthrough: Fore is what a golfer shouts to warn people of a ball in flight.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by function: an apron-like garment worn over clothes to keep them clean.

entries.clue: Concert hall’s not performing lyrical work (3)

indicators.note: ON, meaning performing, is taken away

annotation.surface: A concert hall is dark, so the lyrical piece is not being played.
annotation.walkthrough: An odeon was an ancient Greek hall for music; the 's is 'is', part of the wordplay.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a formal poem of praise, lyric in form, is a lyrical work.

entries.clue: Substitute outstanding artwork (6)

blocks.note: a person who takes over a shift from someone
sculpture that stands out from its background

annotation.surface: A replacement for a brilliant painting.
annotation.walkthrough: Outstanding means literally standing out: a relief is carved so it projects from its surface.
annotation.definitionFit: Two senses: a stand-in who takes over a shift, and sculpture raised from a flat background.

entries.clue: Plant in ground established grip (8)

annotation.surface: A plant rooted in the soil has established a firm hold.
annotation.walkthrough: Plant in ground means bury, as with a body, not gardening.
annotation.definitionFit: A noun sense: a story's grip on you is the hold it has on your attention.
